title: Extract a clean dataset from a messy wiki table
prompt:
hydro_2023.html is a page saved from our internal energy wiki. I need its "Hydroelectricity by country" table as clean JSON. We get a fresh snapshot of this page every year, so I want a reusable script, not a one-off conversion.

Write extract.py so that `python extract.py <page.html> <out.json>` writes the dataset, then run it to produce hydro_2023.json from hydro_2023.html. Standard library only: parse with html.parser (no BeautifulSoup, lxml, pandas, etc.).

Output is a JSON array with one object per country row, in page order, like:

{"region": "Asia", "country": "China", "capacity_mw": 367720, "generation_gwh": {"2022": 1303200, "2023": 1226000}, "share_pct": 13.5}

Rules:
- `region` comes from the Region column (one region cell spans several rows).
- Text should be what a reader sees on the rendered page: no footnote/reference markers ([1], [a], [p], *, † ...), no hidden sort keys, no flag images, whitespace collapsed, HTML entities decoded.
- Numbers are JSON numbers: remove thousands separators (commas or non-breaking spaces), `%` signs and annotations such as `(est.)`. `capacity_mw` is an integer.
- `generation_gwh` has one entry per year column under the "Generation (GWh)" heading, keyed by the year as shown in the header. The set of years differs between snapshots.
- Missing values (blank, a dash, n/a) become null.
- Leave out subtotal and total rows, and ignore the other tables on the page.
